route: self-describing item codes (exemption) + route 1 published per-condition means + route 4 implied parameter (front-surface pixel area vs mean speed estimate)
evidence: Code derivation is exempt (the IRW item IS the .sav column name: the processing script melts the 48 '@' columns by name), and the car tokens are self-describing abbreviations of the paper's eight named vehicles; item_text is blank for all 48 rows, so no wording mapping is at risk. What was checked instead is what the code's four fields mean, since the public_note asserts them: undoing resp = estimate - speed token reproduces every published figure in Klatt et al. (2016) 'Speed estimations' -- overall 45.18 vs 45.2 (range 10-100 vs 'between 10 and 100'); insel 44.19 vs published centre island 44.2 and trottoir 46.17 vs pavement 46.2; speed tokens 45/50/55 give 40.69/45.36/49.49 vs 40.7/45.4/49.5; low-power {nis,vw,kia,toy} 45.71 vs 45.7 and high-power {bmw,alf,merc,chr} 44.65 vs 44.7; small-front {nis,kia,merc,chr} 46.85 vs 46.9 and big-front {vw,toy,bmw,alf} 43.51 vs 43.5; and r(@ prefix, per-car mean estimate) = -0.848 with p = .0078 across 8 cars vs the paper's r = -.848, p = .008, which pins the @ prefix as the measured front-surface pixel area. Only 2 of the 40320 possible relabellings of the car token satisfy all five statistics; the surviving rival (nis<->merc swapped, vw/alf/bmw permuted) is ruled out by the abbreviations themselves. NOT established by the statistics alone: that 'nis' is the Nissan rather than the Mercedes -- that rests on the self-describing-code exemption.
